#Text=CardDAV does not fetch address book from Google Workspace and fails to use existing OAuth2 credentials
#Text=User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/112.0
#Text=Steps to reproduce:
#Text=1. Setup a new Google Workspace account using OAuth2.
#Text=- Calendar and Addressbook permissions are sought by Thunderbird and granted by user
#Text=- Address book is not auto discovered

#Text=2. Add a CardDav address book manually using the Location format specified in [Google Developer docs](https://developers.google.com/people/carddav)  `https://www.googleapis.com/carddav/v1/principals/firstname.lastname@company.org/lists/default`
#Text=3. OAuth2 Addressbook permissions sought again and approved
#Text=4. Address book seemingly added
#Text=Actual results:
#Text=1. Address book does not use existing OAuth2 credentials (and there's no way to choose credentials from a drop down in case multiple OAuth2 accounts exist) that were fetched during email setup
#Text=2. Address book does not display any contact information in the compose window.
#Text=Searching in the compose window address book pane yields nothing
#Text=3. Cannot download the address book in the Address Book tab either
#Text=Expected results:
#Text=I should be able to search for and fill in addresses from the compose window
#Text=I should be able to download all addresses for use offline and synchronise changes between Thunderbird and Google.
#Text=Improve error reporting on non-standard kerberos names
#Text=The kerberos RFC does not declare any restriction on
#Text=characters used in kerberos names, though
#Text=implementations MAY be more restrictive.
#Text=If the kerberos controller supports use non-conventional
#Text=user names *and the kerberos admin chooses to use them*
#Text=this can confuse some of the parsing.
#Text=The obvious solution is for the enterprise admins to "not do that"
#Text=as a lot of things break, bits of hadoop included.
#Text=Harden the hadoop code slightly so at least we fail more gracefully,
#Text=so people can then get in touch with their sysadmin and tell them
#Text=to stop it.
#Text=Note: given the kerberos admin is implicitly a superuser, being
#Text=able to create malformed principal names.
#Text=doesn't give them any privileges, just offers a different way
#Text=to stop the cluster working.
